description:
AI use for this mod?
Yes, heavy. I have more fun this way. This was not a "one-shot prompt" Twitter demo. If that turns you off I understand, but I'm not changing the way I work to be less fun for me.

What is Marines Mod:
This is my attempt at creating an action RTS layer within the universe and confines of the starsector game. I initially started a lot more ambitious than what I have now and quickly realized just how much content was required to do it justice. Longer term it could grow into a generalized ground battle system where the player could choose to playout market attacks, delve ruins in the far off reaches of space, or see what faction vs faction ground combat could look like with low, mid, and high tech forces having their own styles. In reality it's just not there yet. It's a lot of content and I've barely scratched the surface getting a low-tech feeling military that might plausibly be Hegemony / Independent forces.

So what is this Narrative campaign?
A new narrative start where you are the commander of a beat up Cerberus, the Second Wind. You don't have any money, 1 fuel, no place to belong, and mouths to feed. Luckily you have 12 marines so you can pick up some contract work delivering the last of the ore dust in the ship to a customer in desperate need of muscle. Hijinks ensue and you go on a multi-planet tour in the Corvus system playing my half baked mission pack and using the sandbox to have an excuse to start small and build a merc outfit.

What's in this release:
v0.1a is a narrative driven mission pack as I build up the tech / skill to be able to do proper faction vs faction missions that people would want to play. Even with AI assisted development there is so much content required to build out factional rosters, map generation, playtesting, balance, and generally making things fun. I was going crazy attempting to do it all in one go and made a bad "Conquest" mode in this mod under DEBUG missions where you can try it out. Generally it just feels like blob vs blob at that scale and I need a lot more work to make it truly fun.

Features?
- Bad VA (skill issue)
- Mediocre RTS gameplay (skill issue)
- Bad writing (skill issue)
- Human and an alien fauna threat for end narrative end content (dev time / amount of content to create issue)
- Marines, Mechs, Vehicles with some tactical line drawing missions and others for fun of just driving a PD laser tank around and zapping things.
- Manual control of marines, mechs, vehicles by pressing TAB to switch into manual control and TAB to switch back to strategic line drawing mode.
- Cinematics: I wondered what it's like to create them. Kind of fun, also maddeningly hard to get "right". Audio and Voices are the weakest portion there and you'll see I tried a few things for visual styles.
- Factions? Hegemony [low tech], Independents, Pirates. In this release you generally work for local corps, scavengers, and independents. You're not at the scale to be on Heg radar or the other factions. You're bootstrapping a merc outfit where you are the tiniest fish in a big pond of factions and only really working around the Corvus system.

You can probably tell I'm hard on myself a bit here - this mod needs a lot more work.

Okay I'll be an Alpha tester
Awesome here's the releases: https://github.com/drkrompe/StarSector-Marines/releases

Support Development
If you do want to support me I've been doing this for fun (around May 2026). Obviously not required - enjoy have fun:
https://ko-fi.com/dillon429

Tips:
- Start a new campaign for this and try the Second Wind campaign option as a new start in the Corvus system. Current gameplay is not worth doing a heavy modded run with it as there's not enough content to make sense for a full sandbox experience currently. Do a single run with this mod, then go back to your normal experience.
- Drag to select units
- Right click and drag to "draw lines" for the squads for move orders. Press 'R' for move fast after move order given (less accurate firing)
- Select and press 'TAB' to enter manual mode - WASD controls, 'SHIFT' for sprint, 'R' for reload (unless energy weapon).
- Alien Fauna missions are at the "end" of the campaign. You can skip missions that are just bad or not fun by using the in mission "cheat" menu and clicking "win".

If you enjoyed this mod you should play:
- Endless War series (flash games)
- MechWarrior 4: Mercenaries
- Starcraft
- BattleTech (2018) RougeTech mod in particular is a favorite.

The above do this content way better than what's currently implemented here, but the twist is new content and in a new narrative universe I would say. Highly recommend these classics.

Performance Feedback
I've been developing this mod with fairly powerful rigs: AMD 9950x3d processor and Nvidia 3080 GPU - also using my Mac M5 laptop. It's quite possible things will get choppy on later missions when zoomed out. I've worked hard to spread load, multi-core, reduce draw calls etc, but there is still quite a bit of taxing squad logic that occurs. I can play most missions at starsector 60FPS limiter, but I do see some dips periodically. I'm sorry if it's too much for your PC - if you have feedback there let me know the mission you were playing and roughly what was happening when it got choppy (example: many vehicles stuck pathing, or hundreds of squads of marines, or even just being zoomed out and seeing the whole battle space) - also letting me know what kind of PC you are using. My mod runs while the game is "paused" aka you are at a planet so that it tries not to burden your normal gameplay experience. Likewise I load and unload resources from the GPU for missions to try to keep VRAM usage down - generally I'm allocating a few 4k textures and filling an atlas and progressive damage/scuff decals.

Campaign Start Demo (v0.1.0-alpha)

UI Update (v0.1.2-alpha)
